decision_triggers: If line_loss_events stays at 1 or more on the S-bend or slalom with this geometry, the cause is still not geometric. Keep geometry fixed and report where on the course the loss begins.
If line_loss_events is 0 on all three tracks but max_error still approaches 0.06 m, the next geometry step is wheel_track 0.12 m for more differential turn authority.
If runs complete but completion_time exceeds 2.5 s, test wheel_radius 0.035 m for more top speed.
integration_questions: At what course position do the S-bend and slalom line losses begin, and what are the sensor readings and the steering signal at that moment?
Does last_direction or a search direction change the S-bend and slalom loss count with geometry held fixed?
Do the outer sensors at +/-0.05 m read near zero on most of the course, and is the controller still steering correctly from the centre sensors?

intent: Hold the iteration 5 geometry unchanged (seven 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.18 by 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg). The S-bend and slalom line-loss events are then attributed to the controller's line_loss handling or the start pose, not to the body. Geometry stays queued: wheel_track 0.12 m only if line loss is zero on all three tracks and max_error still nears 0.06 m; wheel_radius 0.035 m only if runs complete and completion_time exceeds 2.5 s.
learning: Iterations 3 to 5 show that the +/-0.05 m span removes oval line loss, that mass between 0.7 and 0.6 kg has negligible effect, and that S-bend and slalom loss persists with every geometry that clears the oval. Record whether the controller-side or start-pose change clears those losses. If not, the next geometry test is wheel_track 0.12 m, the only geometry lever left for bend overshoot.
rationale: The last race (iteration 5 design, scored 53.69) gave oval line_loss_events 0, but S-bend and slalom each logged 1.0 line-loss event, with max_error about 0.062 to 0.066 m and progress of 0.16 and 0.11. The authorised feedback rule says that if S-bend and slalom line loss is still 1 with geometry unchanged, the loss is not geometric, so geometry should not be edited. The geometry evidence supports this. With sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, 16 mm footprints and a 0.0205 m detection radius per sensor (half tape width plus half footprint), the seven sensors overlap at 0.015 to 0.02 m pitch. Their combined coverage spans about +/-0.07 m of centre offset, which is beyond the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the array should not drop below the 0.05 sum threshold at any offset the robot can reach while still on the course. Mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg changed max_error and progress by under 0.002 m and 0.01, and body_width cannot move the 0.06 m limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + bw/4) stays at 0.06 m for bw of 0.12 m). The wheel_track 0.12 m change is only triggered if line loss is zero on all three tracks, which is not the case. The wheel_radius change is only triggered if runs complete, which they have not. I therefore hold the iteration 5 geometry exactly, so this race isolates the controller and start-pose work. Expected result: the score stays near 54 to 55 unless the Integrator clears the S-bend and slalom losses, in which case progress on those tracks should rise sharply.
